cleared.check: Task 1 (L-1281): the journal of the shipped op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 x86-64 binary (sha256 9345f48a35156572599c9a183094b0a017a81d9e54a1daecdc249366d15bd745, image revision 65e80332, the build that Unichain, Ink and Soneium answered with on 2026-11-27) lifted from the handlers of cycle 32 down to the tables, with no source model in between.
cleared.result: All 17 instruction tables of the binary were listed and their storage handlers followed by objdump; every routine below ran from its own disassembly in the x86-64 model of cycles 27 to 30, loaded on demand from its .eh_frame range. Two context families were run. Family A, table 0x5aea7c0: SLOAD 0x457ef30 -> host sload 0x4585e50 -> account lookup 0x4a4e6e0 (hashbrown probe over 0xa8-byte buckets, 16-byte SSE2 groups, folded-multiply hash of the 20-byte address with a per-map seed and the global seed word 0x5b8c328) -> sload_concrete_error 0x457a560 -> slot entry 0x44e83f0 (0x68-byte buckets) and storage table growth 0x41395a0/0x4139f40; SSTORE 0x457f080 with the touch entry (tag 2), sstore_concrete_error 0x457a2e0 (StorageChanged tag 8 with the previous value at entry+0x38) and the refund routine 0x2b3c900; TLOAD 0x457fc00 -> TransientStorage get_value 0x297cc70; TSTORE 0x457fc90 -> JournalInner::tstore 0x44e65b0 (two-level map, inner insert 0x4a64d80, rehash 0x4a4f450 and 0x4a4cb20, journal Vec grow 0x4786470 -> finish_grow 0x4164700); checkpoint 0x4579590 (log_i, journal_i and selfdestructed_i at inner+0x10/0x28/0x40, depth at inner+0x118); checkpoint_commit as the saturating decrement 0x4571114-0x457112a of the frame return routine 0x4570fd0, which commits when the result byte is below 5 (Stop, Return, SelfDestruct, Suspend) and calls checkpoint_revert otherwise; checkpoint_revert 0x44daef0, which truncates logs and the selfdestructed list, sets the journal length to journal_i and calls JournalEntry::revert 0x4a4dd50 (jump table 0x9c82ac, 12 arms) on each drained 0x58-byte entry newest first, with the StorageChanged arm restoring present_value through the storage lookup 0x4a4e800 and the TransientStorageChange arm re-inserting or removing through 0x4a64d80 and 0x4a4e910. Family B, table 0x5a0e458 (the table cycle 32 ran): SLOAD 0x1e9d700, SSTORE 0x1e9e530 -> 0x2f5ac60, TLOAD 0x1e9e380, TSTORE 0x1ea4290 -> 0x2d07f50, sload_concrete_error 0x477b730, checkpoint_revert 0x2d07000; 0x2d07000 equals 0x44daef0 and 0x2d07f50 equals 0x44e65b0 instruction for instruction with addresses masked. The account table, every storage table, the two-level transient table, the journal Vec and the depth were real hashbrown and Vec structures in model memory, built, grown and rehashed by the lifted code; only the jemalloc entry points (malloc, mallocx, rallocx, realloc, sdallocx, checked for sized frees), memcpy, memmove, memset, bcmp and the database read below the journal were Python. The first account record of each of three test addresses was placed by Python at the bucket the lifted lookup then found. One dynamic call sits on the path: family A reads the database through call [vtable+0x30] on the fat pointer at host+0x590/0x598 with the key byte-swapped to a B256, which is StateProvider::storage on a boxed trait object; the vtable is chosen at run time by the provider reth opens, so no single relocated vtable belongs to it, and that call is the database read that was stubbed. The other dynamic call in checkpoint_revert (call [rax+0x20] at 0x2d07187) is the drop of a log data buffer and is not reached without logs. No routine had to be modelled from revm source.

cleared.check: Which context the op-reth table of cycle 32 belongs to.
cleared.result: Table 0x5a0e458 belongs to a context whose database reads are compiled out: its sload_concrete_error 0x477b730 inserts a zero slot without any call, and an SLOAD in the model returns 0 whatever the stubbed database holds. In world-chain v2.8.2, whose symbols name each context, the first table at the same position is the EmptyDBTyped context and the block execution contexts are built on State<StateProviderDatabase<...>>; the op-reth names are inferred from that and from the missing database call. The cycle 32 arithmetic results still cover every op-reth table: the 24 arithmetic, comparison and shift handlers other than EXP are the same function in all 17 tables, and the three EXP copies 0x1e8ba00, 0x1e8bb70 and 0x457bdf0 differ from 0x1e8b890 only in the host offset of the gas parameter pointer (0x720, 0x5b0, 0x440).

cleared.check: Task 2 on op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4: 5244 nested-frame sequences through family A (spec byte 13, seeds [35101, 35102, 35103, 35104]), 311 with spec byte 12 (seed [35401]) and 1011 through family B (seed [35301]), with the PoolManager shapes.
cleared.result: No mismatch and no model error in any run. Family A: 33027 checks after 15322 reverts and 12461 commits, every one comparing the journal length, the depth, the original and present value of every slot in the tables and every transient word with a transcription of the revm 43 journal rules, and the final reads, storage and transient words with pyevm.py running the same sequence as bytecode (CALL into three accounts and DELEGATECALL); 0 pyevm mismatches. The SStoreResult of every SSTORE (original, present, new) was read at the return of sstore_concrete_error and equals the rule transcription, so the original value the SSTORE gas and refund read is right after every inner revert. The named shapes ran in every batch: a slot written back to its original value, a slot written twice in one frame, the first read of a slot after an inner revert that wrote it, a write in a committed frame inside a reverted frame, the lock, the nonzero delta count and a delta written with reverts at depth 1, 2 and 3, 40 and 110 new slots and transient keys in one frame (growth of empty storage, transient outer and inner tables and the journal Vec inside the frame, with 87 percent load), and three accounts. Random sequences draw from the journal_seq.py slot set of cycle 32 (Lock.sol, NonzeroDeltaCount.sol, CurrencyReserves.sol, CurrencyDelta.sol keys and the pool state at POOLS_SLOT 6) up to depth 4. Family B ran the same checks against a zero database. Every mismatch record would be in the output files; there are none.

cleared.check: Task 3: the five planted faults in in-memory copies of the lifted code of op-reth family A, op-reth family B and Base.
cleared.result: All 15 planted runs were caught, each fault site executed (hit counts recorded): a StorageChanged revert that restores zero (0x4a4e1a4/0x4a4e1a8 and Base 0x831cd84/0x831cd88), a revert that restores the committed original value in place of the pre-frame value (same sites, loads from the slot record), a checkpoint_revert that skips the newest entry (journal length minus one before the multiply at 0x44daf9b, 0x2d070ab and Base 0x35be41b), a checkpoint whose journal index is one high (0x457959a and Base 0x4dcf7da), and a table probe that stops one group early in the slot entry routine and in the revert lookup (0x44e84d9/0x4a4e8e9 and Base 0x4e2add9/0x831d3a9). The probe fault is caught only by the dense 110-slot sequence, where keys live beyond their first group; the others by the first named sequences.

cleared.check: Task 4: Base v1.5.6 (revm 42.0.1) x86-64 binary (sha256 3cef5ab3fc6234c1020d11f7166e49a6f8a3d9a62f353a0be63c99483ea03fb4; mainnet.base.org answered reth/v2.5.2-9e380dd/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/base/v1.5.6 on 2026-11-27): where its journal code differs from op-reth, and the same lift and runs.
cleared.result: Base has 28 instruction tables. With addresses masked, TransientStorage get_value (0x31b2ff0), JournalInner::tstore (0x35c0bf0), the account lookup (0x6c1fce0), the slot entry routine (0x4e2acf0), finish_grow (0x6a50ca0) and checkpoint (0x4dcf7d0) are instruction for instruction the op-reth routines. JournalEntry::revert 0x831c930 matches 556 of 561 instructions (scheduling and one argument setup of an insert call differ, same jump table arms), and checkpoint_revert 0x35be370 differs in register allocation and in the end-of-iterator niche, tag 0x0c in place of 0xff, which is the variant count of the revm 42 JournalEntry; both were run. The context layout differs (journal inner at host+0x590, target address at interp+0x80, gas at +0x188, spec at +0x1c1, gas parameters at host+0x730). Table 0x91562b0 reads storage through State<DB>::storage 0x6a6dd30, the revm-database cache and bundle layer, which was stubbed with Ok(value). 3033 sequences (seeds [35201, 35202, 35203]): 19651 checks after 9208 reverts and 7410 commits, no mismatch, no pyevm mismatch, no model error. The five planted faults were caught.

The v2.8.1 rehash was not run in the model; it is a new lead. mainnet.optimism.io answered op-reth/v0.0.0-dev-unknown/x86_64-linux, so which build OP Mainnet runs is still not pinned.

cleared.check: Task 6: what in src/ would compute or decide something else if the client journal restored a wrong value, given these results.
cleared.result: Nothing differs. The PoolManager keeps the lock (Lock.sol:8), the nonzero delta count (NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:9-32), the deltas (CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39) and the synced currency and reserves (CurrencyReserves.sol:11-29) in transient storage and pool state, positions and ERC-6909 balances in storage; unlock requires the count to be zero before relocking (PoolManager.sol:103-113), and a failed hook call reverts the PoolManager call (Hooks.sol:131-137). Every inner revert in the lifted op-reth and Base journals restored each of these words to its pre-frame value, kept committed writes of inner frames until an outer revert, and left the original values right, so a hook, token or callback that reverts an inner frame cannot leave pool state changed while the deltas that pay for it are undone on these builds. This holds for the builds whose journal was lifted (op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 and Base v1.5.6). The journal of world-chain v2.8.2 and of conduit-op-reth v2.5.1 was not lifted; on World Chain, Zora and OP Mainnet a live call with a state override showed inner reverts restoring the transient and storage words.

leads.question: Run the op-reth v2.8.1 transient inner-map rehash 0x4bb3fd0 and the reserve routines 0x4bb17d0 and 0x4bb1180 in the model with growing transient tables, as rethj.py does for v2.10.0-rc.4.
leads.why: They are the only journal-side bodies of v2.8.1 that differ from the lifted v2.10.0-rc.4 code beyond register allocation, and v2.8.1 is one of the builds behind OP Mainnet.

leads.question: Run an op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 State-backed context (for example table 0x5a0fc58 with sload_concrete_error 0x477cb10 and its State and block access list layer) through rethj.py, and the 1019-byte revert caller 0x2d06750.
leads.why: The op-reth runs used the boxed state-provider context and the empty-database context; Base ran a State-backed one, but the op-reth State-backed sload variants share only 271 of 648 instructions with the variant that ran.

leadResults.answer: Lifted from the shipped op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 and Base v1.5.6 x86-64 binaries: SLOAD, SSTORE, TLOAD and TSTORE handlers, account and slot lookups, slot insert and growth, the StorageChanged, StorageWarmed, AccountTouched and TransientStorageChange writers, the transient two-level map, checkpoint, the frame commit and checkpoint_revert with JournalEntry::revert, on real tables in model memory. 6566 op-reth and 3033 Base nested-frame sequences with the PoolManager shapes match the revm journal rules after every commit and revert and pyevm.py at the end; the five planted faults are caught on both. v2.8.1 has the same journal routines. Inner reverts restore the pre-frame values and the original values of every slot the sequences write.

world-chain v2.8.2 (revision 95963111) was pulled anonymously. Its arithmetic handlers and jump analysis are compiled differently from op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4, so they were run themselves: 323997 arithmetic cases and 510 jump-analysis programs, no mismatch, planted faults caught. No public image of conduit-op-reth v2.5.1-8f0ccac can be pulled without a token. The World Chain journal is a new lead.
